heading: JSON Escape and Unescape
subtitle: Turn JSON into one escaped string, or an escaped string back into readable JSON, in your browser; nothing is uploaded.
intro: A free JSON escape and unescape tool: open or paste a JSON document and escape it into a single string, with every quote, backslash and line break written as \", \\ and \n, ready to put inside another JSON field, a log line or a test. Or open an escaped string, the kind copied from a log or an API response, and unescape it back into JSON you can read, format and check. Your file never leaves your device.

stepsTitle: How to escape or unescape JSON online

steps.title: Open or paste your JSON
steps.text: Choose a .json file, drop it on the page, or paste the text. An escaped string (it starts with a quote) can be pasted as it is.

steps.title: Escape or unescape
steps.text: The page offers the right step for what you opened: Escape for a JSON document, Unescape for an escaped string. Both are also in the More menu, and Undo takes either back.

steps.title: Copy or download
steps.text: Copy the result from the text pane or download it as a .json file. Unescape again if the string was escaped twice.

handlesTitle: What the JSON escape and unescape tool handles
handles: Escaping: the whole document becomes one JSON string, with quotes, backslashes, tabs and line breaks escaped and non-ASCII text kept as it is.
Unescaping: a document that is a single string holding JSON becomes that JSON again, shown as a tree and as formatted text.
Strings escaped twice or more: unescape once per layer, with undo after each step.
Long numbers such as IDs keep every digit when they are escaped and unescaped.
After unescaping, the usual JSON tools: format, validate, sort keys, query with JSONPath, convert to CSV, Excel, YAML or XML.
limits: It escapes or unescapes the whole document; a single string field inside a larger document is not unescaped on its own.
Unescape needs the string to hold valid JSON; for plain text inside quotes, Repair or the text pane is the way.
faqTitle: Questions about escaping and unescaping JSON

faq.question: Is my file uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Your JSON is read, escaped and unescaped by your browser, on your device, and is never sent anywhere. You can check it yourself: open your browser's network panel and you will see no upload.

faq.question: What does escaping JSON mean?
faq.answer: Escaping turns a JSON document into a single JSON string: every quote becomes \", every backslash \\ and every line break \n, so the document can be stored inside another JSON value, a database field or a log line without breaking it.

faq.question: How do I unescape a JSON string from a log or an API response?
faq.answer: Paste the string here with its surrounding quotes, or save it as a .json file and open it, then choose Unescape. The JSON inside becomes the document, ready to read, format and check.

faq.question: The string was escaped twice. What do I do?
faq.answer: Choose Unescape again. Each Unescape removes one layer of escaping, and Undo takes a step back if you go one too far.

faq.question: Can I unescape just one field of a larger document?
faq.answer: Not yet: Escape and Unescape work on the whole document. Copy the field's value from the tree, paste it here on its own and unescape it.

faq.question: Is it really free?
faq.answer: Yes. There is no account, no watermark and no limit on how often you use it.
